disease_hierarchy_method: Eligible child evidence belongs to the selected general category. Parent-direct estimates are preferred within each overlapping study/population; otherwise one adjusted/primary child estimate is selected. Disjoint populations require explicit documentation.

studies.Reference: Community water fluoridation and health outcomes in England: a cross-sectional study.
studies.Title: Community water fluoridation and health outcomes in England: a cross-sectional study.
studies.Authors: Young N, Newton J, Morris J, Morris J, Langford J, Iloya J, Edwards D, Makhani S, Verne J
studies.Population: Standard small areas and administrative districts in England

effect_size.excerpt: There was no strong evidence of an association between fluoridation and hip fracture, Down syndrome, all-cancer, all-cause mortality or osteosarcoma. Fluoridation was negatively associated with the incidence of renal stones (7.9% lower; 95% CI-9.6%,-6.2%; P < 0.001) and bladder cancer (8.0% lower; 95% CI-9.9%,-6.0%; P < 0.001).

comparison.excerpt: There was strong evidence of lower prevalence of dental caries (P < 0.001) among children living in fluoridated areas

design.excerpt: Community water fluoridation and health outcomes in England: a cross-sectional study.

continent.excerpt: Six million people in England live in areas where the level of fluoride in water is adjusted

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Ecological level exposure to fluoridated water was estimated for standard small areas and administrative districts in England using Geographical Information Systems and digitized boundaries based on known patterns of water supply.
